text:
Aisha K.: Hey folks — during the nightly canary I saw a spike in OOMs on long-context GPT runs. Looks like when seq_len > 4k we pick cuBLASLt for FFN and Triton/FlashAttention combos for attn, but workspace demand climbs and triggers transient OOMs. Anyone else?

Tom: Yep saw that. Perf profiler shows a lot of small allocations around FFN entry/exit. The kernel selector is favoring cuBLASLt because measured matmul throughput is slightly better for mid-head sizes, but peak memory is higher.

Ravi: I reproduced locally with the microbench. Runs with --seq=6144 and batch=2 hit transient OOM on slot allocation step. Dumped allocator trace:
```
ALLOC 0x7f3a... size=24MB type=workspace temp
FREE  0x7f3a... size=8MB
ALLOC 0x7f3b... size=40MB type=kv_cache
OOM when trying to alloc 64MB for FFN_out
```

Aisha K.: Good repro. We need a heuristic that avoids switching to cuBLASLt when it would push working set over headroom. Idea: compute a "slot-scaling" projection per-request: projected_ws = base_ws + f(seq_len, heads, d_model) + reserved_transient. If projected_ws > gpu_headroom * throttle_factor => prefer Triton/Flash path even at small throughput cost.

Tom: +1. Also we should tighten the transient reserve mechanism. Currently reserve fraction = 0.12 global, but that's static and doesn't account for kv cache pressure. When KV cache present we should multiply reserve by kv_penalty.

Priya: Can we try a tuned config? Example: adjust transient to 0.08 normally, and when kv_cache_keys > 0 set transient = 0.08 + min(0.12, 0.000015 * kv_keys * seq_len). Also limit per-request workspace cap: cap = max(estimated_ws, min(estimated_ws, 0.6 * gpu_free)).

Ravi: Test command I ran:
```bash
./microbench --model gpt-3-mini --seq 6144 --batch 2 --kernels flash,triton,cublaslt --alloc-telemetry=on
```
Output snippet (trimmed):
```
kernel_choice: triton (attn), cublaslt (ffn)
est_ws: 1.1GB
kv_cache: 512MB
transient_reserve: 0.12GB
gpu_free_before: 2.3GB
attempt alloc 1.6GB => OOM
```

infra-bot: deploy/canary ws-heuristic-v2 reported 7 failures in ams-1. Logs: https://ci.internal/canary/1716719999

Marcus: Re: allocator tuning — we should prefer buffer reuse for short-lived workspace allocations. Pooling buckets by size-class and lifetime hint would cut churn. Also consider soft-eviction: if a new workspace allocation would cause OOM, try evicting LRU non-essential pooled buffers (not KV cache) up to a threshold before falling back to a different kernel.

Tom: We already track buffer age in slab allocator. Adding lifetime hint from kernel selector is feasible. Kernel selector can attach "workspace_lifetime_hint": short|medium|long. Then allocator can preferentially reuse short-lived pool entries.

Aisha K.: Good. Let's put an experiment plan: 1) short-term: change selector to bias against cuBLASLt when projected_ws > 0.7 * gpu_free; 2) medium-term: implement lifetime-hints + pool reuse; 3) telemetry: emit workspace_headroom_ratio and kernel_choice per-request and add alert when OOM rate > 0.1% over 15m.

Priya: For the short-term bias, we should roll as canary to 10% traffic in region ams, then 50% if stable. I'll own the rollout.

Ravi: I'll add the microbench harness variant that can simulate mixed kv cache occupancy and measure peak transient allocations. Plan to run overnight and post results by EOD.

Marcus: I'll prototype allocator changes — expose an API: reserve(size, lifetime_hint) and try_evict_before_alloc(size, threshold). Will instrument with counters: evicted_bytes, reclaimed_bytes, failed_allocs.

Tom: Quick config snippet for selector bias (P0 patch):
```json
{
  "kernel_selector": {
    "bias_against_cublaslt_if": "projected_ws / gpu_free > 0.7",
    "slot_scaling_fn": "alpha*seq + beta*heads + gamma*d_model",
    "transient_multiplier": 1.0
  }
}
```

Aisha K.: Sounds good. Priya -> rollout. Ravi -> microbench. Marcus -> allocator prototype. Tom -> patch selector and add lifetime_hint. I'll schedule a sync tomorrow 10:30am. :white_check_mark:

Tom: One more note — watch for perf regressions in p50 latency. If we prefer Triton/Flash for more cases p50 might increase slightly; ensure Optimize recommendations don't flip for latency-sensitive routes.

Priya: Noted. We'll gate by per-route SLOs.

infra-bot: canary/rollout ws-heuristic-v2 started: https://ci.internal/rollouts/1716720100

Aisha K.: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the microbench results.
